best_for: PHP developers on Laravel, Symfony or WordPress projects who want debugging, tests and database work in one paid IDE instead of a pile of editor plugins.

points.title: Made for PHP frameworks
points.text: It gives code completion, generation and navigation for Laravel, Symfony and WordPress, as well as plain PHP. JavaScript and TypeScript are covered too, and a database tool talks to MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB and SQLite. A full-stack PHP project rarely needs a second editor.

points.title: Xdebug without the guesswork
points.text: PhpStorm can configure and check Xdebug for you, then step through code and evaluate expressions. Remote debugging over SSH and profiling are included. Test runners for PHPUnit, Pest, Behat, Codeception and phpspec are built in, with code coverage.

points.title: Paid after a 30-day trial
points.text: The download includes a 30-day trial key. Individuals pay USD 109 for the first year, 87 for the second and 65 from the third, or USD 10.90 per month. Organizations pay USD 289 per user per year or USD 28.90 per month. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Twelve months buys a fallback copy
points.text: After 12 straight months on a yearly plan or monthly renewals, you keep a perpetual license for the version that was current when the subscription began. It gets no later updates, and cancelling within that first year forfeits it.

points.title: It wants a capable machine
points.text: JetBrains asks for a 4-core x86_64 or arm64 CPU, 8 GB of RAM with 3 GB free for the IDE, and 10 GB of disk. Supported systems are Windows 10 and 11, macOS 26 and 27, and Linux with GNOME or KDE Plasma and glibc 2.28 or later. Java comes bundled.

points.title: The Flatpak is a community build
points.text: Flathub marks the Linux Flatpak as unverified and says it is not supported by JetBrains. JetBrains itself recommends its Toolbox App, which also handles updates, rollbacks and side-by-side versions, or the .tar.gz download.

points.title: Downgrades are easiest on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 90 versions, with x64 and Arm64 installers for one user or the whole machine. macOS (Intel and Apple silicon) and Linux list only the current release, so an older build there needs the Toolbox App or another source.
